summary: Arkansas fire lookout in Conway County, listed in the Ozark National Forest and dated to 1937; no source gives its design, staffing or present state.

events.note: Forest Lookouts gives 1937 as the year the lookout was constructed; no builder or design is named

evidence.supports: Cedar Mountain is in Conway County
Cedar Mountain listed under Conway County - Ozark National Forest
After the 1910 fire the Forest Service adopted a new rule
evidence.quote: As a result of this fire, the Forest Service put in place a new rule

evidence.supports: Early detection became a priority after the 1910 fire rule
evidence.quote: Early detection suddenly became a priority.

evidence.supports: The 1910 fire was a major fire (largest forest fire in recorded U.S. history)
evidence.quote: In 1910, a fire called the “Big Blow-Up” burned three million acres in Washington, Idaho, and Montana, killing eighty-seven people in what is believed to be the largest forest fire in recorded U.S. history.

evidence.supports: CCC built 3,100 towers during the Depression, many in Ouachita and Ozark-St. Francis national forests
evidence.quote: During the Great Depression, the Civilian Conservation Corps (CCC) built 3,100 towers, including many in the Ouachita and Ozark-St. Francis national forests.

evidence.supports: Arkansas Forestry Commission set up in 1931 and built many towers
evidence.quote: The Arkansas Forestry Commission was established by Act 234 in 1931, and it too built many more towers.

evidence.supports: Watchers often lived in or near their towers and scanned for smoke
evidence.quote: Tower watchmen often lived alone in or near the tower and spent the daylight hours scanning the forests for signs of smoke.
they were equipped with a telephone to report it.

evidence.supports: Watch-tower detection was the main way fires were found until the 1960s (the source's 'this' read as tower-based watch detection)
evidence.quote: This was the primary way of detecting fires until the 1960s, when aerial detection became more accurate and easier.

notes_for_editor: Only one date (1937) and a county and forest listing exist. Checked NHLR (no Cedar Mountain entry), firetower.org FFLOS (no entry found), firelookout.org (Arkansas data still under construction), Preserve Arkansas (no entry) and the Encyclopedia of Arkansas (general history only). No photos found. Status, access, staffing and design stay unknown. The record's coordinates (35.458, -92.7185) come from Forest Lookouts and are unverified. The Encyclopedia material is general context and does not say this tower was built by the CCC or the Forestry Commission. The Encyclopedia's 'this' in the telephone passage is read as tower-based watch detection, the primary method until the 1960s.
